item.title: Indigenous tech solution targets fish losses with data driven farming
item.description: By Cynthia Alo High feed costs, fish mortality and inefficient water management are reducing the profitability of fish farming in Nigeria, prompting calls for wider adoption of technology that can help farmers improve production and cut losses. One such innovation is Smart Pond, developed by Pysis Technologies, an agritech startup using Internet of Things (IoT) technology and artificial intelligence to help fish farmers make production decisions based on actual pond conditions rather than assumptions. The technology monitors pond conditions and provides information to guide feeding and water management, addressing practices that often result in excessive feed use, poor water quality and avoidable fish deaths. Chief Executive Officer and Co-founder of Pysis Technologies, Oluwatoyin Ogundeji, said fish farmers still rely largely on assumptions to determine when to feed their fish or change pond water, leading to unnecessary production costs. He said: “Feed is already expensive, yet we still see about 15 to 20 per cent feed wastage, largely because farmers feed fish when their metabolism is low without knowing.” According to Ogundeji, farmers using the solution could reduce fish mortality by up to 89 per cent, while operating costs can reduce by as much as 10 per cent. He added that assessment of some farmers using the technology recorded profit margins of up to 55 per cent, compared with the 20 to 25 per cent he identified as the average for smallholder and mid-scale farmers. The device has a built-in aerator that supplies oxygen to pond water, allowing farmers to extend the period between water changes and reduce energy costs associated with pumping and replacing water. However, Ogundeji said the adoption of aquaculture technology also depends on addressing institutional challenges, particularly the policy classification of inland freshwater fish farming. He called for a review of the policy that moved inland freshwater aquaculture from the Ministry of Agriculture to the Ministry of Blue Economy, stressing that the change has made it difficult for aquaculture-focused agritech businesses to access some agricultural interventions and support programmes. According to him, more than 80 per cent of Nigerian fish farming takes place on land through freshwater ponds and tanks, making the subsector closely linked to agriculture through its dependence on land, agricultural feed inputs and local food production. He noted that while marine capture fisheries and offshore mariculture fall under the Blue Economy, inland freshwater aquaculture should remain connected to agricultural policies and support systems. To address farmers’ concerns about adopting unfamiliar technology, Pysis said it conducts demonstrations and refresher training through its Thriving Aquaculture Africa initiative. item.title: Ministry presents Zamfara budget performance report
item.description: The Zamfara State Ministry of Finance has presented the 2025 Budget Performance Report, highlighting how funds were utilised in the year under review. The Commissioner for Finance, Muhammad Bello Auta, presented the report during the 2025 budget performance and accountability meeting held at the Finance Ministry Multipurpose Hall in Gusau. Represented by the State Accountant General, Ali Akilu Muhammad Bungudu, the commissioner said that the 2025 Zamfara State Budget, tagged “Rescue Budget 2.0,” was approved at a total of N546,014,575,000. He said the budget was designed to focus on key sectors, including security, education, healthcare and agriculture, among others. Mr Auta maintained that approximately 72% of the total budget was allocated to capital expenditure, while about 28% was earmarked for recurrent expenditure. He also said that the report captured the amount of revenue generated from various sources and the amount spent from the approved budgetary allocations. He further explained that the ministries, departments and agencies that received funds, projects and programmes implemented with the allocated funds, and the level of implementation of major projects were all contained in the 2025 budget report. The commissioner also said that in line with the government’s efforts to promote transparency and accountability in the management of public funds, the Q4 2025 Budget Performance Report was published on 28th January 2026, providing important information for assessing the implementation and performance of the 2025 budget at the end of the fiscal year. He enumerated the projects and programmes identified by the government as beneficiaries of the 2025 budget, including the Gusau International Airport, Gusau-Magami-Dansadau Road, school projects, a modern medical research centre, Smart City, food production initiatives, hospitals, the Gusau International Conference Centre, the Gusau International Sports Centre, as well as road projects across various local government areas, adding that there was an important distinction between what was provided for in the budget and what was actually spent or implemented. item.title: Zamfara monarchs harp on sustained prayer for peace
item.description: The Emir of Gusau, Abdulkadir Ibrahim Bello, has called for constant prayers for the sustenance of peace and stability in Zamfara and Nigeria. He made the call in Gusau on Sunday at the grand ceremony organised by the emirate to honour the emir after receiving a Staff of Office and official recognition as traditional ruler from Governor Dauda Lawal. During the event, district heads, council members of the emirate, community and religious leaders from the emirate, with their subjects, paid homage and solidarity visits to the Emir over his coronation and receiving the Staff of Office from Governor Dauda Lawal. The emir urged the people of the emirate to avoid committing sinful acts that could attract the wrath of God. He called on the people to always fear God and devote themselves to praying to Almighty Allah to address the security challenges in the state. “My message to you is that you should always be law-abiding and live peacefully with one another for the development of peace and economic growth,” the Emir said. He commended Governor Dauda Lawal for his kind gesture and honour to the traditional institution. Meanwhile, the Emir of Birnin Yandoto in Zamfara, Alhaji Aliya Garba-Marafa, tasked his subjects on unity and peaceful coexistence. In a statement issued in Gusau on Sunday by the Chairman, Publicity Committee of the emirate, Nasiru Biyabiki, the monarch made the call while addressing his subjects in Yandoto after receiving the Staff of Office from Governor Dauda Lawal. According to the statement, the event was attended by district heads, council members of the emirate, religious and community leaders, among other stakeholders from within and outside the emirate. He also urged community leaders and district heads in the emirate to maintain peace, foster unity and avoid acts of injustice. item.title: Sultan is a beacon of unity and stability – Governor Lawal
item.description: Governor Dauda Lawal of Zamfara State described the Sultan of Sokoto, Alhaji Muhammad Sa’ad Abubakar III, as a humble leader who brings people together and provides stability. On Monday, the governor attended the 13th Shaikh Usmanu Bin Fodiyo Week and the 20th anniversary of the coronation of Sultan Sa’ad, at the International Conference Centre in Sokoto. This year’s ceremony, with the theme ‘Reviving Ethical Leadership and Social Harmony: Lessons from Sokoto Jihad Leaders’, brought together notable figures from Nigeria and beyond. In his goodwill message, Governor Lawal said the government and people of Zamfara State have been greatly inspired by the Sultan’s wisdom, guidance, and steady leadership, especially during difficult social and security times. He said, “With immense joy, respect, and gratitude to Almighty Allah (SWT), on behalf of the government and people of Zamfara State, I congratulate His Eminence Alhaji Muhammad Sa’ad Abubakar III, 20th Sultan of Sokoto and leader of the Ummah, on the historic 20th anniversary of his coronation. “We remain deeply grateful for your recent presence and support at our coronation and presentation of staff of office to our 19 Emirs in Gusau, which further underscores your commitment to strengthening the traditional institutions across our region. “This year’s celebration reminds us that the Sokoto Caliphate’s legacy transcends borders. Its enduring values, knowledge, justice, moral discipline, responsible leadership and human dignity remain relevant to today’s challenges. “Closer to home in Zamfara State, this legacy carries a particularly compelling message. At a time when insecurity, moral decline, poverty and youth vulnerability threaten our communities, we must draw inspiration from the teachings of Sheikh Usmanu Dan Fodiyo to promote peace, justice, education and social responsibility.” Earlier, the Sultan thanked everyone who played a part and contributed during his 20 years as Sultan of Sokoto. He encouraged religious, traditional, and community leaders to work even harder to promote peace. item.title: Ekiti chiefs pledge one million votes for Tinubu in 2027
item.description: By Rotimi Ojomoyela ADO-EKITI – The Association of Ekiti Traditional Chieftaincy Title Holders has pledged to mobilise one million votes for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid in the 2027 presidential election. The association made the pledge at a gathering hosted by the Managing Director of the Federal Housing Authority (FHA), Hon. Oyetunde Ojo, where traditional title holders from across Ekiti State expressed support for Tinubu’s administration and called for sustained implementation of its policies. The Chairman of the association, Chief Oluwole Ogunsakin, said the one-million-vote target represented its commitment to mobilising communities across the state ahead of the election. He said the association’s network extended to towns, villages, families and grassroots organisations, adding that members would encourage eligible voters to participate peacefully and freely in the electoral process. Ogunsakin also identified insecurity as one of the major concerns confronting residents, saying traditional rulers and chiefs were strategically positioned to contribute to grassroots security because of their closeness to the people. He welcomed ongoing legislative discussions on the establishment of state police, expressing optimism that the proposal would eventually become law. The association urged the government to consider involving traditional chiefs in screening and recommending credible candidates from their communities for recruitment into the proposed state police structure. Ogunsakin said such involvement would strengthen public confidence in the security system, given traditional leaders’ knowledge of their communities and local security challenges, including activities around farmlands. He said: “As custodians of our heritage and respected community leaders, we recognise the importance of peaceful democratic participation and constructive political engagement. “On this occasion, the Association of Ekiti Traditional Chieftaincy Title Holders declares its commitment and aspiration to mobilise one million votes through our communities in support of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu in the 2027 presidential election, while supporting your political mobilisation efforts. “We shall encourage eligible voters to participate peacefully and make their choices freely at the ballot box.” Speaking at the event, Ojo described the Tinubu administration’s infrastructure projects, particularly road construction, as unprecedented, comparing their scale to infrastructure development during the administration of former Head of State, General Yakubu Gowon. He said the roads being constructed under Tinubu’s administration were designed to last between 30 and 40 years. Ojo also commended the President’s appointments, saying they reflected fairness and representation across the country’s ethnic groups. item.title: Security: Traditional rulers critical partners – Lawal
item.description: Governor Dauda Lawal said the traditional institution is an important partner in promoting peace, stability, and development. The governor revealed this at the weekend when he presented staff of office and official vehicles to 19 emirs in Zamfara State. The coronation and presentation ceremony took place at the Trade Fair Complex in Gusau, the state capital. Among the dignitaries in attendance were the Sultan of Sokoto, the Etsu Nupe, and the Emir of Gwandu. Following their oaths of office, Governor Lawal presented staff of office to 11 first class emirs and eight second class emirs. Each newly coronated emir also received a GAC ULTRA SUV (2025/2026 model), a MIKANO ZNA HILUX vehicle, and an EV ANTIQUE MODEL car (DDP). The vehicles are intended to support their travels and help them engage more closely with their communities. In his remarks, Governor Lawal said the ceremony reflected his administration’s recognition of the traditional institution as an enduring part of society and an important partner in promoting peace, stability, and development. He noted that the ceremony also reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to giving traditional rulers the recognition and institutional support they need to carry out their responsibilities effectively. item.title: Abia: How one woman ended Okuenyi mothers’ dangerous trek for childbirth
item.description: …Govt promises standard facility By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — For pregnant women in Okuenyi community, Obingwa Local Government Area of Abia State, the journey to motherhood was often a painful test of endurance, one that began long before labour pains set in. With no functional health facility to attend to them, expectant mothers had to trek approximately three miles to neighbouring communities in search of antenatal care and safe delivery. For some, the journey was a desperate race against time, with the lives of both mother and child hanging in the balance. But one woman who grew up in the community could no longer bear the sight of her people enduring such hardship. Moved by the plight of the women, Mrs Ebere Ulelu-Obiesie, an indigene of Okuenyi, stepped in to change the narrative, sponsoring the renovation and upgrading of the community’s dilapidated temporary health post and equipping it with essential medical facilities. Her intervention, complemented by financial support from Rev. Friday Nnah, Proprietor of Abundant Living Christian School, Okuenyi, has brought renewed hope to a community whose women had for years faced the agonising prospect of travelling miles to access basic healthcare. For the women of Okuenyi, the renovated facility which was inaugurated recently, represents much more than refurbished walls and newly acquired medical equipment. It offers the possibility of receiving medical attention closer to home and, perhaps, a safer journey into motherhood. Painful reality that inspired intervention Narrating the circumstances that prompted the intervention, Mrs. Ulelu-Obiesie told SEV that her attachment to Okuenyi, where she was born and raised before marriage, made it impossible for her to turn her back on the suffering of her people. She disclosed that the decision to rehabilitate the health post was driven by her worry over the deplorable condition of the facility and the difficulties pregnant women in the area pass through to access healthcare. According to her, a visit to the health post with her husband, Mr Ernest Obiesie, exposed the gravity of the situation and strengthened her resolve to intervene. “I was born in Okuenyi before I got married. I could not stand by and watch my people continue to face these difficult challenges, especially in accessing healthcare services. Pregnant women, in particular, were exposed to enormous difficulties. “After visiting the former health post in Okuenyi with my husband and seeing its deplorable condition, I resolved to liberate my people from these challenges by initiating the project through my husband, in collaboration with my co-sponsors,” she said. Her husband, Ernest, revealed that he initially hesitated when she presented the proposal, citing financial constraints. However, seeing the condition of the health post during a subsequent visit changed his perspective, as the couple resolved to respond to the community’s urgent healthcare needs. item.title: Soludo: Peter Obi and I are friends, but differ politically
item.description: By Vincent Ujumadu AWKA – Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, has described the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Mr Peter Obi, as a close friend, saying their differences are largely rooted in their contrasting political views and ambitions. Soludo, a former governor of the Central Bank of Nigeria, stated this in an interview with the BBC Igbo, where he explained that both families maintained cordial relations despite their political differences. He said Obi’s wife was the godmother of his daughter, while his wife served as the confirmation godmother to Obi’s daughter. “Peter Obi and I are very good friends. Our two families have cordial relationship. His wife is the godmother of my daughter and my wife is his daughter’s confirmation godmother,” he said. The governor, however, said they were on opposite sides of the political contest and had different visions. “But on the issue of political contestation, we are fighting for our positions. I have a different vision and he has his own vision,” he added. Soludo recalled that when he contested the Anambra governorship election, Obi had supported another candidate, but said he held no grudge against the former governor over the development. “When I contested for governorship, he had his favoured candidate, but by the grace of God, I prevailed and I am not holding it against him,” he said. On the 2027 general elections, Soludo said he was not opposed to Obi contesting for the presidency but questioned the prospects of an opposition candidate defeating an incumbent president without a united opposition platform. “You could not defeat the president when he contested from outside, is it now that he is the president and seeking re-election that you will defeat him? This is not about emotion,” he said. The governor also recalled that in March 2022, before the 2023 presidential election, he had encouraged Obi to contest on the platform of the All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA). He said his suggestion was intended to enable Obi to mobilise support among the Igbo and subsequently form alliances with other political groups to pursue power at the national level. “In March 2022 at Nnamdi Azikiwe University, before he contested in 2023, I wanted him to contest on the APGA platform, not because he would win, but to use it to galvanise Igbo people and then go into alliance with others to seek for power,” Soludo said. He argued that winning a Nigerian presidential election required building political alliances beyond one region. “You don’t win Nigerian election by being the champion of only one part of the country,” he added. item.title: Ika South council boss urges Alisimie to back APC
item.description: ….Says voting strength determines community’s political influence By Victor Ahiuma-Young The Chairman of Ika South Local Government Area, Delta State, Engr. Jerry Ehiwarior, has urged residents of Alisimie communities to mobilise support for the All Progressives Congress (APC), saying their voting strength could influence the community’s political relevance and access to development projects. Ehiwarior made the call while speaking as Special Guest of Honour at the Alisimie Able Youths Summit held at Idumukwu Primary School, Alisimie. He urged the youths to take an active role in shaping the political future of their community, stressing the need for collective participation in the electoral process. Among the dignitaries at the summit were the APC House of Assembly candidate, Mrs Cordelia Anyagwu; Ika South APC Chairman, Comrade Frank Izekor; Prof. Pally Agidi; Dr Donald Peterson; Chief Peter Idion; Dame Caroline Agbi; Comrade Jonathan Ojobu; Chief Dennis Araro; Mr Jonathan Onwuka; Ambassador Lucky Omorojie; APC Ward 3 Chairman, Madueke Egede; and Chief Peter Momah. The council chairman said Alisimie must position itself strategically within the political process to secure what he described as its rightful share of government attention, development and opportunities. He also urged the youths to take the message beyond the summit by engaging their elders on the importance of political participation and collective action. Ehiwarior appealed to residents to vote for all APC candidates in the forthcoming elections, arguing that a united voting pattern would strengthen the community’s political standing and improve its prospects of attracting development interventions from the local and state governments. According to him, the number of votes delivered by a community could influence its place in the state’s political calculations and its ability to attract government projects. “I encourage the youths to recognise the political value of their numerical strength and mobilise residents towards a common political position. Organised participation is essential for communities seeking greater influence in governance,” he said. Ehiwarior commended the Alisimie Able Youths for organising the summit, describing it as a demonstration of youth leadership, political awareness and commitment to the community’s future. He said bringing residents together to discuss their political future was an important step towards building the unity and collective strength needed for meaningful participation in the democratic process. item.title: ASUU backs Taraba varsity lecturers, demands strike resolutionBy
item.description: Femi Bolaji JALINGO – The Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU), Yola Zone, has declared solidarity with lecturers of Taraba State University (TSU) over their ongoing strike, describing their grievances as legitimate and demanding immediate implementation of the 2025 Federal Government-ASUU agreement. The union also urged the Taraba State Government to stop delaying the implementation of the agreed remuneration framework and settle outstanding arrears owed to the university’s academic staff. The Zonal Coordinator of ASUU, Comrade Dani Mamman, stated this while addressing journalists after an expanded congress meeting of the union in Jalingo. Mamman criticised the state government for what he described as unnecessary administrative delays, insisting that the grievances of the university’s lecturers deserved immediate attention. He said the zone’s support for ASUU-TSU was based on the principles of justice, equity, collective responsibility and the protection of the legitimate rights and entitlements of academic staff. The Yola Zone comprises seven public university branches across Adamawa, Borno, Taraba and Yobe states. They are Adamawa State University, Mubi; Federal University Gashua; Kashim Ibrahim University, Maiduguri; Modibbo Adama University, Yola; Taraba State University, Jalingo; University of Maiduguri; and Yobe State University, Damaturu. Mamman faulted the state government for placing Taraba State University lecturers in a different position from their counterparts in other universities in the region, urging it to end further delays. He said a report by the Taraba State Government’s fact-finding team, presented to ASUU on September 24, 2026, established that the universities covered by the exercise had fully implemented the 2025 FGN/ASUU agreement. According to him, the finding was particularly significant because other universities in the zone had adopted the payment tables provided under the agreement without undergoing similar fact-finding exercises. He said the state government had no justification for subjecting ASUU-TSU to further administrative processes after completing its verification exercise in August 2026. Mamman also expressed concern over what he described as endless computations by the government, particularly its consideration of alternative implementation levels of 95, 98 and 100 per cent after the verification exercise had been concluded. He maintained that consultations, negotiations and computations had been completed, leaving no reason for further delays. The zonal coordinator demanded the immediate and full implementation of the agreed remuneration framework without setting up additional committees or conducting further verification exercises. He also called for the settlement of all accumulated arrears based on the financial computations submitted by the tripartite committee. item.title: Obi exhausted from campaign schedule, but in good health — NDC
item.description: The Deputy Spokesperson of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) Presidential Campaign Council, Sam Omale, has said the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, is in good health, attributing concerns about his condition to exhaustion from a demanding campaign schedule. Omale said Obi had been advised to take some rest following hectic engagements involving frequent travels between cities and attendance at multiple political activities. He spoke on Channels Television’s The Morning Brief on Tuesday while responding to concerns about Obi’s health, particularly after his recent campaign rally in Enugu State, where he reportedly indicated plans to take a break. The campaign council’s deputy spokesperson described Obi as being in good health, insisting that the exhaustion would not affect his campaign activities. “If you know the person of Mr Peter Obi, he is so passionate for this country and he is pouring out his life. Sometimes, I wonder where he gets his energy from,” Omale said. “Today, he is in London this night; the following morning, he is in Enugu. The exhaustion comes in. A human being is a human being. “But he is in perfect health; nothing is wrong with him. It is just exhaustion, and we are trying to calm him down to take a sleep.” He said Obi often combined several activities at the same time, including attending engagements, answering questions and responding to emails. According to him, the former Anambra State governor would continue with town hall meetings before the commencement of the main campaign rallies. “So, it is pure exhaustion, which definitely has no impact on the campaign we are conducting. He is going to continue the town halls before the main rallies begin. He is fine,” Omale added. However, the NDC National Publicity Secretary, Osa Director, said he was unaware that the party’s presidential candidate had experienced exhaustion arising from campaign activities. Director, who said he had spent time with Obi in Bayelsa State, maintained that he had no knowledge of any health-related incident involving the presidential candidate. “I knew nothing happened to Peter Obi. Honestly, I am not being sarcastic here. As far as I am concerned and as far as I know, Peter Obi is with his health,” he said. He added that he was with Obi in Bayelsa for a day and learnt that the presidential candidate had travelled abroad, noting that some people had accompanied him to the airport. “So, I don’t know where the story of exhaustion came from. So, Omale is in a better position to elucidate the point he has made,” he said. Director further said the national campaign council had not taken any steps to ask Obi to slow down his activities, adding that he was unaware of any development that would require such intervention. item.title: Tinubu graduated with first-class in accounting — Education minister
item.description: The Minister of Education, Tunji Alausa, has defended President Bola Tinubu’s academic record at the Chicago State University, insisting that the President graduated with a first-class degree in accounting from the American institution. Alausa said he was familiar with the university, having lived in Chicago for almost 30 years, and had personally met several people who studied with Tinubu. He stated this during an interview on Channels Television on Tuesday while responding to questions about the President’s educational qualifications. “I’m telling you hardcore facts. I lived in Chicago for almost 30 years. I’ve been to that university so many times,” he said. Asked whether he had met Tinubu’s classmates, the minister replied, “Oh, many, many, many, in person. Many. So forget the nonsense of…” When asked whether the President graduated with a first-class degree from the institution, Alausa answered, “In accounting, of course.” He also described Tinubu as a genius, dismissing questions about the President’s intellectual capacity. “Oh, he’s a genius. Let’s not talk about the capability of this President. President Bola Ahmed Tinubu is literally a genius,” he said. The minister further defended Tinubu’s performance in office, claiming that the President had transformed Nigeria from a moribund country into a growing economy. “Look at how he’s transformed a moribund country three years ago to a country that is growing,” Alausa said. However, when the interviewer challenged the description by pointing to the country’s out-of-school children and poverty levels, the minister insisted that the conversation should remain focused on the President’s achievements. “Let me focus on what you’re saying. I don’t want you to derail this conversation. But this President has delivered this for Nigeria,” he added. Tinubu’s academic qualifications have continued to attract public scrutiny, particularly following the controversy surrounding his Chicago State University records during the 2023 presidential election petition. The debate resurfaced in August 2026 after the Independent National Electoral Commission began displaying the personal particulars and academic credentials submitted by presidential candidates for the 2027 general elections. item.title: 2027: Akume’s allies disown Alia’s campaign council as Benue APC supremacy war deepens
item.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi A fresh supremacy battle has erupted in the Benue State chapter of the All Progressives Congress, APC, following the rejection of about 500-man campaign council for President Bola Tinubu and Governor Hyacinth Alia by the Benue Strategic Alliance for Tinubu 2027, a political mobilisation platform associated with the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, SGF, Senator George Akume. The disagreement followed Monday’s announcement by the APC State Organising Secretary, James Ornguga, of a joint campaign council for Tinubu and Alia ahead of the 2027 general elections. The party also fixed Thursday, November 5, for the inauguration of the council in Makurdi, with a supplementary list expected to be released later. However, the Benue Strategic Alliance for Tinubu 2027, in a disclaimer issued Tuesday and signed by its Director-General, Chief Akange Audu, disowned the purported campaign structure, alleging that the names of its conveners, members and political candidates had been included without their authorisation. The Alliance specifically faulted the inclusion of its conveners, Senator Jack Tilley-Gyado, and Elder Simon Shango, as well as its candidates for the National Assembly and Benue State House of Assembly, in the list of the purported Alia campaign council. It stated, “for the avoidance of doubt, the Benue Strategic Alliance for Tinubu 2027 categorically dissociates itself from the said publication and disowns any claim or suggestion that the individuals mentioned therein are associated with, or constitute members of, the purported Alia Campaign structure.” The group further questioned the political arrangement that reportedly placed Governor Alia as chairman of the campaign council while listing Akume, whom it described as the founder and foremost political leader of the APC in Benue State, as merely a member. According to the Alliance, “We find it particularly contentious that a purported Alia Campaign structure would designate Governor Hyacinth Alia as its Chairman while listing the Founder and foremost political leader of the APC in Benue State, Sen. George Akume, Secretary to the Government of the Federation, SGF, merely as a member.” The Akume-aligned group alleged that “since the APC secured victory in the 2023 general elections, the party’s established leadership and structures have, in practical terms, been sidelined by the Alia administration. This has contributed to the divisions and disagreements currently affecting the party in the state.” Despite rejecting the campaign council, the group insisted that “the Benue Strategic Alliance for Tinubu 2027 remains committed to its stated mandate of mobilising support for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s re-election in 2027. “Our political engagement also extends to supporting APC candidates for the National Assembly and the Benue State House of Assembly who emerge from the list and leadership direction recognised by our leader, Sen. item.title: Rising feed costs threaten poultry, livestock farming in 3 states
item.description: Farmers in Niger, Kogi and Nasarawa states have warned that rising feed costs, expensive day-old chicks and poor market prices threaten livestock production and livelihoods. They said the situation had forced some operators to reduce production, sell their animals at losses or abandon farming altogether. The farmers spoke in separate interviews with the News Agency of Nigeria on Tuesday during a nationwide survey in Minna. They identified high feed costs, which account for 70 to 80 per cent of poultry production expenses, as their biggest challenge. They called for subsidised feed ingredients, affordable financing, improved access to essential inputs and local feed mills to reduce production costs. In Kogi, a poultry farmer and retired Federal Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security director, Mr Dare Olukaiyeja, said feeding accounted for 80 per cent of his production costs. Olukaiyeja, who keeps 250 birds, said a crate of eggs currently sold for about N6,200 amid declining consumer purchasing power. Similarly, Mr Shola Adeyi, a Lokoja-based farmer with a 1,000-bird capacity, said feed prices had increased by N2,000 to N3,000 per bag almost monthly since January. He said starter, finisher and layer feeds sold for N22,500, N22,000 and N16,000 respectively, while day-old chicks cost about N2,200 each. Adeyi identified unreliable electricity, extreme heat and high bird mortality as additional challenges confronting poultry farmers. He said some operators had abandoned the business because they could not afford alternative power sources. He said eggs sold for between N6,000 and N6,500 per crate, while broilers fetched N4,500 to N5,000 per kilogramme. According to him, the prices barely covered production costs, necessitating long-term subsidised or interest-free loans and effective market regulation. Another farmer, Mr Malik Ajayi, said day-old chick and feed prices usually increased during Sallah, Easter and Christmas. Ajayi, who rears broilers, cockerels and foreign turkeys, said he recently bought three cartons of day-old chicks for N352,500. He attributed some price fluctuations to possible exploitation by large-scale producers and urged the government to introduce effective price regulation. Ajayi, who keeps 150 broilers, 50 cockerels and 15 foreign turkeys, said some farmers sold their birds cheaply to avoid prolonged feeding costs. He added that frozen poultry dealers also faced high electricity and preservation expenses. Mrs Oluwaseyi Fadaka, another Lokoja-based farmer, said a bag of feed now cost about N22,000, with her 40 Noiler birds consuming one regularly. She said rising feeding costs were eroding profits, forcing farmers to sell at losses or abandon the business. Fadaka said some smallholders were exploring organic feeding alternatives but needed government support through subsidised feed and affordable, quality inputs. item.title: JP Morgan’s Nigeria expansion to boost foreign investment — IMPI
item.description: By Joseph Erunke, Abuja The Independent Media and Policy Initiative (IMPI) has said the planned expansion of global financial giant JP Morgan Chase into Nigeria’s merchant banking sector could attract fresh foreign investments, improve corporate financing and strengthen the country’s access to international capital markets. The policy think tank said the American financial institution’s application for a national merchant banking licence was a significant endorsement of Nigeria’s investment prospects and could encourage more multinational corporations to commit long-term capital to the country. In a policy statement signed by its Chairman, Dr Omoniyi Akinsiju, IMPI said the proposed expansion could reshape Nigeria’s corporate finance landscape by making it easier for businesses to access funding, structure large-scale projects and manage risks associated with cross-border investments. According to the group, JP Morgan’s transition from a representative office to a fully licensed merchant bank would enable it to deepen its involvement in trade finance, corporate lending, cross-border underwriting and other sophisticated financial transactions. It said the development could be particularly beneficial to capital-intensive sectors such as energy, telecommunications and manufacturing, where high borrowing costs and complex financing arrangements had continued to constrain investments. “JP Morgan Chase’s move to secure a national merchant banking licence in Nigeria marks a significant shift in West Africa’s corporate finance landscape,” IMPI said. The group added that the proposed operations could help multinational companies structure investments more efficiently through direct access to cross-border trade facilities, commodity hedging instruments and syndicated financing involving domestic and international markets. It said the availability of such services could reduce delays and additional costs businesses often encounter when relying on multiple financial intermediaries to execute major projects. IMPI also argued that Nigeria’s sovereign and corporate borrowers could benefit from stronger links to international capital markets, while the presence of a major global financial institution could reinforce confidence among foreign pension funds, sovereign wealth funds and private equity investors. However, the think tank cautioned that JP Morgan’s proposed entry would not automatically translate into increased foreign direct investment, stressing that the broader benefits would depend on prevailing investment conditions and the consistency of economic policies. Tinubu’s reforms and investor confidence The policy group attributed renewed international interest in Nigeria to the economic policy direction of President Bola Tinubu’s administration, particularly the foreign exchange market reforms and removal of petrol subsidy introduced in 2023. item.title: Champions League: Man United rise from the dust to shock Roma 3-2
item.description: Manchester United roared back from 2-0 down to give beleaguered manager Michael Carrick a lifeline with a memorable 3-2 win over Roma at Old Trafford. The unrest among the home fans bordered on mutiny after Roma surged into a 2-0 lead inside 20 minutes through Matias Soule and Donyell Malen. But Matheus Cunha’s struck twice after a twice-taken Bruno Fernandes penalty had given United hope to end a nine-game winless run in all competitions. The decision to hand Carrick a stay of execution looked to have backfired in a lifeless first half United performance. Roma, though, failed to slay their ghosts of previous trips to Old Trafford in another spectacular Champions League collapse. Gian Piero Gasperini’s lost 4-3 to Real Madrid last month after leading 3-1 with just eight minutes remaining. The Italians have now lost on all five visits to the Theatre of Dreams, most notably when Carrick scored twice in a 7-1 thrashing in the Champions League quarter-finals 19 years ago. Carrick reacted to Lisandro Martinez’s foolish red card in a 2-0 defeat at Chelsea on Saturday by dropping the Argentine international. It made little difference as his disorganised defence was torn apart inside the opening 20 minutes. Soule was afforded acres of space to control Rodrigo Mora’s pass and slot past Senne Lammens on 11 minutes. Moments later United were left completely exposed again down their left and Soule’s shot hit the outstretched hand of Ayden Heaven. Malen converted the resulting penalty for his 12th goal of the season. The game was temporarily stopped midway through the first half by supporters throwing tennis balls onto the field, accompanied by chants calling for with United’s unpopular owners, the American-based Glazer family, to sell the club. United were dealt a further blow inside two minutes of the second half when £70 million ($94 million) signing Carlos Baleba pulled up with a suspected severe hamstring injury after bursting into the Roma box. Yet, Carrick’s luck turned just before the hour mark when Cunha won a generous penalty award for minimal contact by Gianluca Mancini. Fernandes’s first spot-kick was saved by Roma’s third-choice goalkeeper Devis Vasquez, but was given a reprieve by encroaching by the visitors. The United captain smashed home at the second attempt to kickstart the comeback. Seconds later Bryan Mbeumo hit the inside of both posts and Roma captain Bryan Cristante had to hack clear off the line as the visitors rode their luck. However, Leonardo Balerdi’s swipe at fresh air deep inside his own box gifted Cunha the simplest task to tap in an equaliser seven minutes from time. Three minutes later, the Brazilian thundered a shot past Vasquez at his near post and flung himself into the crowd in what proved to be a costly celebration. Cunha was booked and then shown a second yellow card moments later for a wild lunge in stoppage time. The 10 men held on to breathe new life into United’s Champions League campaign after back-to-back defeats

item.title: Inter End Champions League Slump With 3-0 Win Over Feyenoord
item.description: Inter Milan got their stuttering Champions League campaign back on track with a comfortable 3-0 win Tuesday against Dutch giants Feyenoord, helped by a superb first-half strike from German defender Yann Bisseck. The three-time champions of Europe had lost their first two group games, but had far too much quality for a disappointing Feyenoord, who had little answer to Inter’s pace and attacking ability. On a clear and crisp evening in Rotterdam, the visitors quickly silenced the ever raucous crowd in De Kuip, piling on sustained pressure that paid dividends as early as the eighth minute. Bisseck was given too much space on the edge of the box, allowed to turn and drill a sumptuous curling left-footed shot low past the diving Tjark Ernst in the Feyenoord goal. Feyenoord struggled to break out of the Inter Milan high press and the Serie A champions dominated possession and territory for much of the first quarter. The home fans had to wait for half an hour before their side produced their first effort of note, a clever one-two playing in Anis Hadj Moussa, who saw his shot blocked. And Inter doubled their advantage shortly afterwards. Feyenoord’s Dutch midfielder #10 Luciano Valente (R) reacts at the end of the the UEFA Champions League, league phase, Matchday 4, football match between Feyenoord and Inter Milan at De Kuip Stadium in Rotterdam on November 3, 2026. (Photo by JOHN THYS / AFP) England international Djed Spence found himself in acres of space on the right hand side. His shot looped up off a defender, allowing Pio Esposito to bundle in with his head from short range. The beginning of the second half brought more misery for Giovanni van Bronckhorst’s men, as Feyenoord’s defence backed off and invited an advancing Piotr Zielinski to shoot. The Polish international midfielder gratefully accepted the invitation, firing home an unstoppable drive off the post on 54 minutes. With the game effectively over as a contest, Inter boss Cristian Chivu rang the changes, bringing off star striker Marcus Thuram. Halfway through the second half, fireworks launched from outside the stadium landed on the pitch and roof, causing a short interruption. And the match itself rather fizzled out, as Inter cruised and Feyenoord failed to find any spark to penetrate the Italian defences. The win saw Inter climb to a more respectable place in the middle of the Champions League table while Feyenoord’s solitary victory leaves them adrift of the knock-out phase. Feyenoord’s next Champions League encounter is a home tie against Porto, while Inter Milan welcome Stuttgart. item.title: Raphinha, Yamal Fire Barcelona To Champions League Win Over Villa
item.description: Raphinha struck twice to propel Barcelona to a 3-0 Champions League win over visitors Aston Villa on Tuesday, ending the English side’s perfect start to the competition. Five-time winners Barcelona took an early lead through Lamine Yamal before Raphinha continued his fine goalscoring form with a second-half brace. Barca bounced back after defeat by champions Paris Saint-Germain in their previous European outing to stay in the hunt for a top eight league phase berth. Unai Emery’s Villa competed well in the first half but were eventually undone by Barca’s greater ability in the final third. The Champions League anthem was not played before the game, as a mark of respect for Tenerife striker Jesus De Miguel, who died on Tuesday morning after an on-pitch collision in a Spanish second division match the previous day, provoking shock across the football world. Villa captain John McGinn had only visited the Camp Nou once previously, on a summer holiday as an eight-year-old, and might have expected better weather than the downpour both teams were subjected to. The skipper might also have expected a more focused start, with Villa handing Barcelona the lead in the seventh minute. Barcelona’s Spanish forward #10 Lamine Yamal (R) and Barcelona’s English forward #17 Anthony Gordon fight for the ball with Aston Villa’s Dutch defender #22 Ian Maatsen (L) and Aston Villa’s Swedish defender #03 Victor Lindelof during the UEFA Champions League 1st round day 4 football match between FC Barcelona and Aston Villa at Camp Nou Stadium in Barcelona on November 3, 2026. (Photo by MANAURE QUINTERO / AFP) The Spanish champions pressed Aston Villa extremely high and Joao Gomes played a poor pass straight to Yamal in his own box. The 19-year-old winger gladly took the gift and stroked past Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki. Villa reacted strongly and Matty Cash had a vicious drive deflected narrowly wide before Joao Cancelo blocked Gomes’s effort. Barcelona goalkeeper Joan Garcia was quick off his line to beat Nicolas Jackson to a dangerous through-ball. Suzuki saved from Anthony Gordon as Villa again struggled to bring the ball out from the back under Barca’s pressing. Garcia was called into action again by Johan Manzambi as the match lurched from end-to-end. Barcelona extended their lead early in the second half when Fermin Lopez fed Raphinha, who showed quick footwork before finding the bottom corner. Cancelo powered a strike narrowly over before setting up Raphinha for Barcelona’s third with a superb cross with the outside of his boot. The Brazil winger, who has made the number nine position his own this season, pounced from close range for his 19th goal of the season across all competitions. Yamal sent a shot skidding wide as Barcelona probed for a fourth. It did not come, but the Catalan giants were able to record a first Champions League clean sheet in 19 games. item.title: Atiku Alleges Plot To Disrupt ADC Campaign In Sokoto, Vows Resistance
item.description: Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has accused the Sokoto State Government and security operatives of working to frustrate the African Democratic Congress (ADC) campaign in the state, alleging that protesters were being mobilised to disrupt the party’s planned rally. Atiku, the ADC presidential candidate, made the allegations at a news conference in Abuja on Tuesday, claiming that the party had been denied access to public facilities and logistical support ahead of the rally. He said the restrictions were part of a deliberate effort to place the opposition at a disadvantage and undermine the right of Nigerians to freely choose their leaders. “These are not harmless administrative delays. They are deliberate attempts to deny the ADC a level playing field,” he said. ﻿ Atiku also alleged that the Department of State Services (DSS) was recruiting protesters to cause disturbances and create a situation that could be used to impose a curfew and prevent the rally from taking place. He identified an office behind Zenith Bank on Koko Road as one of the locations where the protesters were allegedly gathered. “We know where some of these protesters are assembled: an office behind Zenith Bank on Koko road. “Trucks are stationed there and dispatched to key points, including the roundabout. These mobilised protesters are causing gridlock. “Commuters are being threatened and, in some cases, beaten. Some of the protesters have moved away from the roundabout to find shade,” he said. The former Vice President accused security personnel allegedly involved in the operation of abandoning their professional duties for political interests. “This is not intelligence work. It is political interference dressed in official uniform. Security agencies exist to protect Nigerians and uphold the law, not to recruit protesters or help a political party manufacture a crisis,” he said. He asked the officers involved to end the alleged mobilisation and discharge their duties without political bias. Turning to the wider political climate, Atiku accused President Bola Tinubu’s administration of attempting to weaken opposition parties by drawing their members into the ruling APC. He described the strategy as one of political absorption and intimidation, warning that its ultimate objective was to leave Nigeria with little meaningful opposition. “The aim is to reduce Nigeria to a one-party state in all but name,” he said. Atiku also faulted the Federal Government’s handling of the economy, pointing to the rising prices of food, transport, fuel and electricity as evidence of the pressure on households. He said the ADC would pursue policies aimed at expanding local production, increasing food supply, generating employment and lowering the cost of doing business if elected in 2027. Among his proposals is a targeted production subsidy linked to fuel refined in Nigeria. He said the measure would ease the burden on consumers while supporting domestic industry. item.title: Seen And Heard At The US Midterm Elections
item.description: Reporters, photographers and video journalists are deployed by AFP across the United States to document the 2026 midterm elections as Americans head to the polls. Here is a round-up of interviews on Tuesday at polling stations where voters agreed to share their thoughts about what was on their minds and motivating their choices. Hopeful Democrats With polling data suggesting the Democratic Party is on track to capture a majority in the House of Representatives and perhaps even in the Senate, many left-leaning voters said they were hopeful about the results. “Two years ago was a really devastating outcome for me,” Emma Mondadori, a 39-year-old who works in philanthropy, told AFP in Brooklyn, New York, referring to President Donald Trump’s election. “I’ve been really looking forward to this day where we get to have a say again in the future of our country… I’m cautiously hopeful, optimistic.” AUSTIN, TEXAS – NOVEMBER 03: Voters wait in line to cast their ballots at the polling place at the Baker Center on November 03, 2026 in Austin, Texas. Chip Somodevilla/Getty Images/AFP (Photo by CHIP SOMODEVILLA / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP) The cost of living With gasoline prices up by a third since last year and diesel nearly double — not to mention sharp food price inflation — everyday spending was on many people’s minds. “It’s about the cost of living, gas prices, those kind of things. It needs to change for the everyday person, and I’m an everyday person,” Donta Comer, a 38-year-old project manager in Atlanta, Georgia, told AFP. Tom, a 27-year-old businessman at the same polling station who declined to give his surname, agreed. “Everyone, at least in my generation, is a little frustrated with the affordability crisis and gas prices and what’s going on abroad,” added the non-partisan voter. Leadership referendum Mid-term elections are typically seen as a form of referendum on the sitting president. And few leaders have polarized public opinion as strongly as Donald Trump. “I’m independent but I voted Democrat, I just wanted to go back into the culture of decency, integrity, honesty, and the rest follows,” Yan Cardineau, 59, told AFP in Austin, Texas. “If we lose that, it doesn’t matter how much money you make.” Atlantans head to the polls to vote on Election Day at Park Tavern on November 3, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. Megan Varner/Getty Images/AFP (Photo by Megan Varner / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP) Estrella Roque, a 69-year-old voter of Cuban origin, told AFP in Miami she had voted Republican. “What I like about the Republicans is that they can fix the country,” she explained in Spanish. “Donald Trump hasn’t been given time to show who he really is.” Immigration In his final pitch to voters, Trump has stressed his success in reducing immigration and stopping crossings along the southern border with Mexico. While his tough stance plays well with his core supporters, others have been put off by the brutal tactics
